title: Nag Hammadi Library (NHL)
language_name: Sahidic Coptic (with Subakhmimic in some texts)
edition_reference: Coptic Gnostic Library (CGL; ed. James M. Robinson, Brill 1975–1995, 5 vols.); Sahidic Coptic transcriptions
license: The Coptic originals (4th C CE manuscripts, discovered 1945) are public domain. Modern critical editions and English translations have varying copyright status — typically Brill's CGL transcriptions are © Brill but the underlying Coptic text is PD.
source_acquisition_status: DECLARATION ONLY — full Coptic text staging deferred. Possible sources for future acquisition: (a) The Nag Hammadi Scriptures, ed. Marvin Meyer (HarperOne 2007) — English; (b) Coptic Gnostic Library (Brill); (c) various academic transcriptions scattered across NHC III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII, XIII volumes. The hand-transcribed Coptic from the manuscript facsimiles is the canonical source.
facsimile_source: Facsimile Edition of the Nag Hammadi Codices (Leiden: E. J. Brill, 1972–1984; 12 vols.)

priority_codices.title: Apocryphon of John (Secret Book of John)
On the Origin of the World
Treatise on the Resurrection (Letter to Rheginos)
Gospel of the Egyptians (Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit)
Apocryphon of James (Secret Book of James)

priority_codices.tradition: Berlin Gnostic Codex; partial — pages missing

main_apparatus.note: Apparatus consists of textual lacunae (the codices have missing pages), variant readings between codices where multiple copies exist (e.g., Apocryphon of John in II,1/III,1/IV,1), and the critical apparatus of the CGL edition.
